@copilot Update this PR directly with a scoped prose and code-comment correction. The user clarified: '"ordinary" isn't really working. I didn't really intend that as a term to use. I was thinking more in terms of the names that they could just be unqualified names For that normal case'.

The default case should simply be called "advice", not given a new mode name. Remove "ordinary" as an advice-mode label throughout the documentation and comments introduced by this PR. Do not mechanically replace it everywhere with "normal", "default", "standard", "non-inline", or "isolated". Keep ordinary prose unqualified and qualify the inline alternative when needed. Where comparing both mechanisms explicitly matters, describe inline = true versus inline = false, or say non-inlined advice. Advice inlining and isolated/injected helper placement remain separate choices; preserve those concrete distinctions and the actual invokedynamic dispatch explanation.

Apply this to docs/contributing/writing-instrumentation-module.md, .github/agents/knowledge/javaagent-advice-patterns.md, .github/scripts/draft-release-notes/rules.md, the two AzureExplicitParentContextHelper Javadocs under instrumentation/azure-core/azure-core-1.36 and azure-core-1.53, the comments in instrumentation/azure-core/azure-core-1.36/library-instrumentation-shaded/build.gradle.kts, muzzle/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/tooling/muzzle/AdviceInspector.java, and the changed comment in javaagent-tooling/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/tooling/instrumentation/indy/IndyTypeTransformerImpl.java. Use "Advice" for the "Ordinary advice" heading and "Configure production advice" for "Use ordinary production advice". State the requirement to set inline = false explicitly, preserving the two internal exceptions and Byte Buddy's inline = true annotation default. For example, the mixing sentence can say "Mixing advice marked inline = true and inline = false disables automatic helper isolation." Keep the Azure compatibility claim valid for both forms, for example "whether or not advice is inlined", and describe the actual loading constraint in its dependency comments rather than naming an ordinary-advice mode. Source comments must describe the current code, not a past migration.

Preserve existing uses of "ordinary" that merely describe helpers or compiled methods and are not advice-mode labels. Keep the unqualified AdviceInstrumentationTestModule and AdviceInstrumentationTest fixture names, advice package, advice-test registration and matcher, all assertions and advice annotations, and the SecurityManager variant deletion unchanged. Do not rename production classes, relocate packages, change dependencies or behavior, touch the other three rename PRs, or rewrite historical changelog entries. Run only applicable targeted formatters/documentation linting for changed files; this follow-up changes prose/comments only, so unrelated behavior tests and builds are unnecessary. Acceptance is that no added prose introduces an "ordinary advice" mode while the precise configuration, dispatch, helper-loading and compatibility explanations remain accurate.
